physical_skill: Pick the loaded launcher up off its flat side, turn it upright and hold it still and level a few centimetres over the stadium's centre with one gripper, while the other gripper takes the ripcord handle and rips the toothed strip straight out along its slot in about a quarter second, so the top is released spinning near 300 rad/s with little tilt or sideways speed, then keep both grippers clear while it spins on its tip for 10 s.
valid_shortcuts: None that score, per the README red-team runs: do nothing 0 (never released); one arm ripping the cord from the launcher lying on the table 0 (launcher dragged, cord out 2 mm); slow 1.5 s pull 0 (released at 59 rad/s, falls in 0.3 s); 45-degree angled pull 0 (cord binds after 5.3 cm, never released). Touching or catching the top ends spin time (5 cm fingertip rule); a ring-out zeroes the trial before 1.0.
distinct_from_nearest: The only spinning-top task on the board (#3166) spins the top by pumping a plunger with the top in hand; the only pull-cord task (#3395) pumps a counter-mounted appliance. Here a free launcher must be held level in the air over a target by one hand while the other makes a single fast, on-axis rip whose speed becomes a released free body's stability. Residual risks: reviewers may see the outcome as covered by #3166 or the hold-and-pull as covered by #3395, and may question real-arm rip speed (#2722 precedent).
